title: Damper Throttling Operating Point Explorer
description: Predict-then-reveal Plotly chart: the learner closes an outlet damper in five fixed steps and, before each new system curve appears, predicts whether airflow and static pressure rise, fall or stay the same; the sim then draws the new system curve and operating point beside the previous one, gives reason-based feedback, and ends with a score, a mastery line and an unscored explore mode.

subject: damper throttling

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Damper throttling and the operating point
learningObjectives: The learner will interpret how closing an outlet damper moves a fan's operating point along its fan curve, predicting the direction of change in airflow and static pressure before each new damper setting is revealed.

accessibility.notes: Chart region has an aria-label and every revealed operating point is also listed in an HTML table; predictions are aria-pressed toggle buttons in labelled fieldsets; verdicts and the summary are announced through FP.announce (aria-live); feedback uses ✓/✗ glyphs with solid/dashed borders; curves differ by colour and dash pattern; the operating point is a diamond and the previous one an open circle. Keys 1-3 choose airflow higher/lower/same, 4-6 static pressure higher/lower/same, Enter closes the damper one step or checks.

controls.label: Close damper one step
controls.purpose: Move to the next damper setting; in the challenge, opens the prediction for that step (Enter)

controls.label: Higher / Lower / Same (airflow)
controls.purpose: Predict the direction of the airflow change (keys 1-3)

controls.label: Higher / Lower / Same (static pressure)
controls.purpose: Predict the direction of the static pressure change (keys 4-6)

controls.label: Check
controls.purpose: Lock the prediction pair and reveal the new system curve and operating point (Enter)

controls.label: Reset
controls.purpose: After Step 5: return to wide open and step freely without predictions

controls.label: Start over
controls.purpose: Clear the score and restart the five-step challenge

equations: System curve: P_sys(Q) = 5.0 × m × (Q / 10,000)² in. wg
rules: m takes 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 6.0 in that order and never decreases during the challenge
Airflow rounded to the nearest 1 CFM and pressure to 0.01 in. wg, halves rounded up
A prediction pair is correct only when airflow is lower and static pressure is higher
Five steps, fixed order, one scored attempt each; mastery is 5 of 5
assumptions: Fixed fan speed; system curve passes through zero flow at zero pressure
limitations: Illustrative curves, not a catalog fan; real fan curves are read from the catalog

sources: All curves and values are illustrative, computed from the chapter 19 spec Rules
Qualitative behaviour (operating point moves to the left of the rating point; horsepower savings usually much less than other methods): FanPedia: The Fan & Blower Encyclopedia, pp. 182-183

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Committed prediction before each reveal, with consecutive operating points kept visible for comparison
keyQuestions: If you close the damper one step, where will the fan operate?
Why does static pressure rise when the damper closes?
Why does airflow fall by much less than the resistance multiplier rises?
commonMisconceptions: Closing a damper lowers the pressure the fan produces.
Closing a damper changes the fan curve.
Airflow falls in proportion to how far the damper is closed.
assessmentOpportunities: Running score 'Predictions correct: n of 5'; mastery is 5 of 5 steps with both directions correct (one attempt per step). Viewing the chart after the reveal is exploration, not evidence.
